svg.title: How Super works
svg.desc: Two speech engines transcribe every chunk in parallel and a word vote merges them. Gemma reads the whole transcript, then rules only on the chunks where the engines disagreed. Everything runs on the Mac.
svg.text: Gemma rules only where they disagree.
How a Super run turns a recording into one transcript. Everything runs on the Mac.
split-track meeting: your mic and the call are recorded apart
the call, via the audio tap
at most 28 s, cut in silence
so no word is lost at a cut
Pass 1: every chunk, three at a time
Gemma stays idle: the engines get the hardware
in parallel, each word with a confidence
e.g. Whisper v3, GPU and ANE
Whisper already drops sign-offs and the
stock lines it writes over its padding
Three chunks × two engines run side by side. Whisper gives
every call its own transcribe task on one shared model.
Gemma rules in pass 2, after the engines are done, so it
never competes with them for the GPU.
How one disputed word is decided
the trusted engine's spelling and punctuation
the trusted engine's Latin beats a native-script guess
from the weak engine dropped, unless 3+ in a row
voted text (shown live), raw A, raw B, agreement
With Max quality off there is no pass 2: a chunk
agreeing below 0.5 goes to Gemma right here,
with only the text before it as context.
Pass 2: Gemma reads first, then rules
plus spelling fixes that pass guards
sees raw A and raw B, the text
Why two passes: most chunks agree and never needed context. Pass 1 runs flat out, and the slow
judgment is spent afterwards, only where the engines fought, with context from both sides.
Measured on a 42-minute meeting: pass 1 was about 96% of the run, pass 2 about a minute. v3.8.0 overlap: 6-min slice 241 s → 183 s.
a call line heard again on your
mic lines are you, the diarizer
labels the others, names from the talk
A chunk over 120 s: the engine is rebuilt and the chunk retried; stuck again, the healthy engine does it alone.
A hung ruling keeps the voted text; an arbiter that cannot be rebuilt is dropped, so the run still finishes.
